title: Details of mitosis vary among close relatives and are not specific to the organism

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Details of mitosis vary among close relatives and are not specific to the organism

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The details of mitosis (presence of visible caryokinesis, position of the field of force, number of chromosome groups, chromosome form and arrangement) vary greatly even among closely related organisms or within one species, and are not specifically related to the organism in which they occur.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. IV: On the Internal Form and Structure of the Cell

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: there seem to be strong grounds for believing that these and many similar phenomena are in no way specifically related to the particular organism in which they have been observed, and are not even specially and indisputably connected with the organism as such.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter IV, “On the Internal Form and Structure of the Cell”; topic “Biological significance of mitotic figures”. Scope: mitosis in plants and animals, e.g. Copepods, Ascaris megalocephala

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch04-14: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.60

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Phylogenetic signal and variance partitioning operationalize the main assertion. Existing images cover many taxa but not a balanced comparative sample, so a restricted rather than comprehensive test is feasible.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Code mitotic traits from standardized images across phylogenetically close and distant taxa, partition trait variance within species, among close relatives, and among major clades, and test phylogenetic signal. Low signal plus high close-relative or within-species variation supports the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The phrase 'not specifically related' lacks a quantitative threshold.

Some listed features require specialist recoding from publications.

Cross-species imaging protocols are heterogeneous.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.75
analysis feasibility: 0.5
operationalizability: 0.65
discriminating power: 0.55
data adequacy: 0.5

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Open count databases can test the chromosome-number slice, including variation among relatives. The rest of the mitotic details Thompson lists, spindle position, chromosome shape and grouping, remain in the cytological literature and would have to be coded by hand. Species-constant chromosome numbers also mean the data can support the claim for some details and cut against it for others.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Quantify mitotic characters, including presence of a visible spindle, chromosome number, chromosome form and arrangement, within species and between close relatives, and test their association with taxonomy. High within-species and within-genus scatter, and weak correlation with species identity, would support the claim; characters that diagnose species or close relatives would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Number is often constant within species, which pulls against a blanket reading.

'Not specifically related to the organism' can be read as several different association tests.

Chromosome number is only one of the listed details; form, arrangement and spindle position are not in these databases.
